h: Turning Lakeside into a Full Day
p: The south end of Windermere is a lovely, slightly calmer part of the lake, and Lakeside makes a great hub for a family day. The smart trick is to arrive one way and leave another. Drive to Haverthwaite, take the steam train down to Lakeside, visit the aquarium, then hop on a lake cruise up to Bowness or Ambleside before heading back. Services on the railway and the boats vary through the year, so check what's running for your dates before you build your plan around them.

Fell Foot, a National Trust park on the southern tip of the lake, sits just across the water and is a brilliant spot for a picnic, a paddle or hiring a rowing boat in the warmer months. Close to Lakeside, Stott Park Bobbin Mill, cared for by English Heritage, shows how wooden bobbins were made for the cotton mills, with machinery that still works. Grizedale Forest, a little further away, is full of walking trails, cycle routes and outdoor sculptures hidden among the trees.

Up in Bowness, families with younger children can visit The World of Beatrix Potter, which brings Peter Rabbit and friends to life, while Windermere Jetty Museum shows off a remarkable collection of historic boats and lake history. At the aquarium itself, an hour or two is about right, depending on how long the kids want to stay with the otters, and it's a calm, cosy place to warm up after time on the water. Bring a jumper for the boat ride. Windermere can be chilly when the wind gets up.
